cards.back: Missing energy in beta decay needed an escaping particle.
accept: Missing energy in beta decay needed an escaping particle.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Which exchange particles mediate the weak interaction at A-level?
cards.back: W⁺ and W⁻ bosons.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Which exchange particle represents the electromagnetic interaction?
cards.back: A virtual photon.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How is a muon classified?
cards.back: A lepton.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why must a kaon produced by a strong interaction have balancing strangeness elsewhere?
cards.back: Strangeness is conserved in strong interactions.
accept: Strangeness is conserved in strong interactions.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What are the electron-lepton numbers of an electron and its antineutrino?
cards.back: +1 and −1 respectively.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Is maximum photoelectron kinetic energy linear with incident wavelength?
cards.back: No. It is linear with frequency, not with wavelength.
accept: No. It is linear with frequency, not with wavelength.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to a photon when an atom emits light?
cards.back: The atom loses energy equal to the photon's energy.
accept: The atom loses energy equal to the photon's energy.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why do atoms produce discrete line spectra?
cards.back: Electrons occupy discrete energy levels.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to de Broglie wavelength if a particle's momentum doubles?
cards.back: It halves.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does increasing accelerating voltage change electron diffraction ring size?
cards.back: The rings become smaller as electron wavelength falls.
accept: The rings become smaller as electron wavelength falls.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the phase difference across one-eighth of a cycle?
cards.back: π/4 radians or 45°.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What phase difference exists across three-quarters of a cycle?
cards.back: 3π/2 radians.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What distinguishes particle speed from wave propagation speed?
cards.back: Particles oscillate locally; the wave transfers energy along the medium.
accept: Particles oscillate locally; the wave transfers energy along the medium.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How are adjacent nodes and antinodes spaced?
cards.back: One quarter-wavelength.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the area under a force–time graph represent?
cards.back: Impulse, equal to change in momentum.
accept: Impulse, equal to change in momentum.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the signed area under a velocity–time graph?
cards.back: Displacement.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: When is the distance on a velocity–time graph greater than displacement magnitude?
cards.back: When velocity changes sign.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does a velocity–time gradient equal?
cards.back: Acceleration.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Which energy store increases when work is done against friction?
cards.back: Internal or thermal energy.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does terminal speed mean for net force?
cards.back: The resultant force is zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How do the opposing drag and driving forces compare at terminal speed?
cards.back: They balance.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the centripetal direction of an object's net force in uniform circular motion?
cards.back: Towards the centre.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to the material after exceeding the elastic limit?
cards.back: It cannot fully return to its original dimensions on unloading.
accept: It cannot fully return to its original dimensions on unloading.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What distinguishes a ductile material from a brittle one?
cards.back: A ductile material undergoes significant plastic deformation before fracture.
accept: A ductile material undergoes significant plastic deformation before fracture.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the unit of Young modulus?
cards.back: Pascal (Pa).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Define conductance.
cards.back: The reciprocal of resistance, 1/R.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is conductance measured in?
cards.back: Siemens (S).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the loss of terminal potential difference due to internal resistance called?
cards.back: Lost volts.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For an ideal cell delivering current, what is its terminal p.d.?
cards.back: Equal to its emf.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the area under an I–t graph give?
cards.back: Charge transferred.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the gradient of a Q–t graph give?
cards.back: Current.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can a filament lamp's resistance rise as it glows brighter?
cards.back: Hotter ions vibrate more and scatter electrons more often.
accept: Hotter ions vibrate more and scatter electrons more often.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What direction is acceleration in simple harmonic motion relative to displacement?
cards.back: Opposite to displacement, towards equilibrium.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: At which point is a simple harmonic oscillator's speed greatest?
cards.back: At the equilibrium position.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Where is kinetic energy zero in ideal SHM?
cards.back: At maximum displacement.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What phase difference is there between acceleration and displacement in SHM?
cards.back: π radians (180°).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the quality of resonance depend on physically?
cards.back: Damping and how close the forcing frequency is to natural frequency.
accept: Damping and how close the forcing frequency is to natural frequency.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the ideal-gas assumption about intermolecular forces?
cards.back: Negligible except during collisions.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the ideal-gas assumption about molecular collisions?
cards.back: They are perfectly elastic.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does absolute zero correspond to for ideal-gas molecular translation?
cards.back: Zero mean translational kinetic energy.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to mean translational kinetic energy if absolute temperature doubles?
cards.back: It doubles.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to temperature during a pure substance's change of state at fixed pressure?
cards.back: It remains constant while latent heat is transferred.
accept: It remains constant while latent heat is transferred.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why must gas-law temperatures be in kelvin?
cards.back: Gas laws require absolute temperature.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is gravitational potential at infinity by convention?
cards.back: Zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why is the gravitational potential around an isolated attractive mass negative?
cards.back: Work must be supplied to move a mass from the field to infinity.
accept: Work must be supplied to move a mass from the field to infinity.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the gradient of an electric-potential graph indicate?
cards.back: Electric field strength with opposite sign in one dimension.
accept: Electric field strength with opposite sign in one dimension.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does one farad mean?
cards.back: One coulomb of charge stored per volt.
accept: One coulomb of charge stored per volt.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does energy stored at fixed capacitance change if voltage doubles?
cards.back: It quadruples.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a charging capacitor, what happens to the charging current over time?
cards.back: It falls towards zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the unit of the RC time constant?
cards.back: Seconds.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: When is the magnetic force on a moving charged particle zero?
cards.back: When velocity is parallel to the magnetic field.
accept: When velocity is parallel to the magnetic field.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to the force on a wire if it is turned parallel to the magnetic field?
cards.back: It becomes zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What physical quantity does a tesla measure?
cards.back: Magnetic flux density.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the meaning of back emf in an electric motor?
cards.back: An induced emf opposing the supply.
accept: An induced emf opposing the supply.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Define activity of a radioactive sample.
cards.back: Number of decays per second.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the SI unit of activity?
cards.back: Becquerel (Bq).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does decay constant represent?
cards.back: Probability per unit time of a nucleus decaying.
accept: Probability per unit time of a nucleus decaying.
reject: time for half the nuclei to decay

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does sample activity change as unstable nuclei decay?
cards.back: It decreases exponentially.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why is a decay process random?
cards.back: The decay of an individual nucleus cannot be predicted.
accept: The decay of an individual nucleus cannot be predicted.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is a unified atomic mass unit?
cards.back: One twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
accept: One twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why are time-of-flight mass-spectrometer ions given the same kinetic energy?
cards.back: So flight time depends on mass-to-charge ratio.
accept: So flight time depends on mass-to-charge ratio.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which ions arrive sooner in a TOF tube at equal kinetic energy: lower or higher m/z?
cards.back: Lower m/z ions.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does a mass spectrum's relative abundance quantify?
cards.back: The proportion of detected ions giving a peak.
accept: The proportion of detected ions giving a peak.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Define a limiting reactant.
cards.back: The reactant used up first, restricting product formed.
accept: The reactant used up first, restricting product formed.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the meaning of one part per million by mass?
cards.back: One unit mass of solute per million units mass of mixture.
accept: One unit mass of solute per million units mass of mixture.
one in a million by mass

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is atom economy different from percentage yield?
cards.back: Atom economy uses balanced equations; yield measures actual versus theoretical product.
accept: Atom economy uses balanced equations; yield measures actual versus theoretical product.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the shape around nitrogen in NH₄⁺?
cards.back: Tetrahedral.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the H–O–H bond angle in water approximately?

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is the H–N–H angle in NH₃ smaller than 109.5°?
cards.back: One lone pair repels bonding pairs more strongly.
accept: One lone pair repels bonding pairs more strongly.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What molecular geometry results from six bonding pairs and no lone pairs?
cards.back: Octahedral, with 90° and 180° bond angles.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does solid sodium chloride not conduct electricity?
cards.back: Its ions cannot move through the lattice.
accept: Its ions cannot move through the lattice.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Define standard enthalpy of neutralisation.
cards.back: Enthalpy change forming one mole of water when acid and base react in dilute solution.
accept: Enthalpy change forming one mole of water when acid and base react in dilute solution.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Define standard enthalpy of atomisation.
cards.back: Enthalpy change forming one mole of gaseous atoms from an element in its standard state.
accept: Enthalpy change forming one mole of gaseous atoms from an element in its standard state.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What must be true for the enthalpy changes in a Hess cycle to sum to zero?
cards.back: They form a complete closed cycle.
accept: They form a complete closed cycle.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does a catalyst not change the position of equilibrium?
cards.back: It accelerates forward and reverse reactions without changing K.
accept: It accelerates forward and reverse reactions without changing K.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does activation energy mean?
cards.back: Minimum energy required for a successful reaction.
accept: Minimum energy required for a successful reaction.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is meant by dynamic equilibrium?
cards.back: Equal forward and reverse rates in a closed system.
accept: Equal forward and reverse rates in a closed system.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does changing pressure not shift an equilibrium with equal gas mole counts both sides?
cards.back: Both sides have the same number of gas molecules.
accept: Both sides have the same number of gas molecules.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is a catalyst absent from an equilibrium-constant expression?
cards.back: Its concentration is not part of the equilibrium state ratio.
accept: Its concentration is not part of the equilibrium state ratio.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the physical meaning of positive entropy change?
cards.back: Greater dispersal of energy or more possible arrangements.
accept: Greater dispersal of energy or more possible arrangements.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does an increase in temperature favour positive-entropy reactions in ΔG?
cards.back: The −TΔS term becomes more negative.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does ΔG < 0 indicate under specified conditions?
cards.back: A thermodynamically feasible change.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does ΔG = 0 indicate at constant temperature and pressure?
cards.back: Equilibrium.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What changes in a rate equation when temperature changes?
cards.back: The rate constant k, not the reaction orders.
accept: The rate constant k, not the reaction orders.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the overall reaction order?
cards.back: The sum of powers of concentrations in the rate equation.
accept: The sum of powers of concentrations in the rate equation.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens to Kp if an equilibrium mixture is compressed at constant temperature?
cards.back: Kp stays constant.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does the sum of exponents in a Kp expression represent?
cards.back: The stoichiometric powers of the gaseous species.
accept: The stoichiometric powers of the gaseous species.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does a more positive standard electrode potential indicate?
cards.back: Greater tendency for reduction relative to the standard hydrogen electrode.
accept: Greater tendency for reduction relative to the standard hydrogen electrode.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the emf of a cell under standard conditions?
cards.back: E°(positive electrode) − E°(negative electrode).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does Ka quantify for a weak acid?
cards.back: Its acid-dissociation equilibrium constant.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does a buffer resist?
cards.back: Large pH changes when small amounts of acid or alkali are added.
accept: Large pH changes when small amounts of acid or alkali are added.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What determines the pH at half-neutralisation of a weak acid?
cards.back: pKa (pH = pKa).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does the melting point fall sharply from silicon to phosphorus in Period 3?
cards.back: The structure changes from giant covalent to simple molecular.
accept: The structure changes from giant covalent to simple molecular.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is argon's boiling point extremely low?
cards.back: Only weak London dispersion forces act between single atoms.
accept: Only weak London dispersion forces act between single atoms.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the acid–base character of aluminium oxide?
cards.back: Amphoteric.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens when acidic oxides react with alkalis?
cards.back: They form salts and water.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the nature of sodium oxide?
cards.back: Basic oxide.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the nature of sulfur dioxide as an oxide?
cards.back: Acidic oxide.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can transition-metal ions form coloured complexes?
cards.back: Partly filled d orbitals allow absorption of visible wavelengths.
accept: Partly filled d orbitals allow absorption of visible wavelengths.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does bidentate mean?
cards.back: Forms two coordinate bonds to one metal centre.
accept: Forms two coordinate bonds to one metal centre.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the charge on a hexaaqua aluminium(III) ion?

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the common colour of aqueous nickel(II) ions?
cards.back: Green.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does a blue precipitate of copper(II) hydroxide indicate?
cards.back: Cu²⁺ in the sample.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What makes two molecules structural isomers?
cards.back: Same molecular formula but different structural formulas.
accept: Same molecular formula but different structural formulas.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What makes a pair of molecules stereoisomers?
cards.back: Same structural formula but different spatial arrangement.
accept: Same structural formula but different spatial arrangement.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What stereochemical arrangement is Z?
cards.back: Higher-priority groups on the same side of the double bond.
accept: Higher-priority groups on the same side of the double bond.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What distinguishes thermal from catalytic cracking in product emphasis?
cards.back: Thermal cracking favours alkenes; catalytic cracking favours fuels and aromatics.
accept: Thermal cracking favours alkenes; catalytic cracking favours fuels and aromatics.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is a termination step important in free-radical substitution?
cards.back: It removes radicals by combining them.
accept: It removes radicals by combining them.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What pollutant is formed by incomplete hydrocarbon combustion?
cards.back: Carbon monoxide, CO.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why do iodoalkanes generally hydrolyse faster than chloroalkanes?
cards.back: The C–I bond has lower bond enthalpy.
accept: The C–I bond has lower bond enthalpy.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What class of organic product arises when a halogenoalkane reacts by elimination?
cards.back: Alkene.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why do chlorofluorocarbon radicals contribute to ozone depletion?
cards.back: Chlorine radicals catalyse ozone breakdown and are regenerated.
accept: Chlorine radicals catalyse ozone breakdown and are regenerated.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is the alkene double bond attacked by electrophiles?
cards.back: The C=C double bond is a region of high electron density.
accept: The C=C double bond is a region of high electron density.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which carbocation is normally most stable: primary, secondary or tertiary?
cards.back: Tertiary.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does the major product of an unsymmetrical alkene addition reflect?
cards.back: Formation of the more stable carbocation intermediate.
accept: Formation of the more stable carbocation intermediate.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the key difference between addition and substitution?
cards.back: Addition combines reactants; substitution replaces a group.
accept: Addition combines reactants; substitution replaces a group.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why are tertiary alcohols resistant to straightforward oxidation?
cards.back: No H atom is bonded to the carbon carrying OH.
accept: No H atom is bonded to the carbon carrying OH.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is a biofuel?
cards.back: A fuel made from recently living biomass.
accept: A fuel made from recently living biomass.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is ethanol from biomass not automatically carbon neutral?
cards.back: Growing, processing and transporting biomass may emit greenhouse gases.
accept: Growing, processing and transporting biomass may emit greenhouse gases.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What absorption range suggests the C=O group in an IR spectrum?
cards.back: About 1680–1750 cm⁻¹.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does the molecular-ion peak help determine?
cards.back: Relative molecular mass of the molecule.
accept: Relative molecular mass of the molecule.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is an IR fingerprint region useful?
cards.back: Its complex pattern can help confirm molecular identity.
accept: Its complex pattern can help confirm molecular identity.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Define a racemic mixture.
cards.back: Equal amounts of the two enantiomers.
accept: Equal amounts of the two enantiomers.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does a racemate not rotate plane-polarised light overall?
cards.back: The equal and opposite optical rotations cancel.
accept: The equal and opposite optical rotations cancel.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the oxidation product of an aldehyde?
cards.back: A carboxylic acid.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What product class forms when a ketone is reduced?
cards.back: Secondary alcohol.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can nucleophilic addition to a planar carbonyl produce enantiomers?
cards.back: The nucleophile can approach from either face.
accept: The nucleophile can approach from either face.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the functional group of an acid anhydride?
cards.back: –CO–O–CO–.
accept: two acyl groups linked by oxygen

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the by-product when an acid reacts with an alcohol to make an ester?
cards.back: Water.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the name of alkaline ester hydrolysis to make soap?
cards.back: Saponification.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does benzene react by substitution rather than addition?
cards.back: Substitution retains the stable delocalised electrons in the ring.
accept: Substitution retains the stable delocalised electrons in the ring.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why are the six carbon–carbon bonds in benzene equal in length?
cards.back: Electrons are delocalised across all six carbon atoms.
accept: Electrons are delocalised across all six carbon atoms.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is phenylamine a weaker base than methylamine?
cards.back: Its nitrogen lone pair is partly delocalised into the benzene ring.
accept: Its nitrogen lone pair is partly delocalised into the benzene ring.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which nitrogen-containing product class forms when a primary amine reacts with an acyl chloride?
cards.back: A secondary amide.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which bond type distinguishes a polyester repeating link?
cards.back: An ester link, –COO–.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which bond type distinguishes a polyamide repeating link?
cards.back: An amide link, –CONH–.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why are many polyesters biodegradable while polyalkenes are not?
cards.back: Their ester links can be hydrolysed.
accept: Their ester links can be hydrolysed.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why are fewer steps often preferred in an industrial organic synthesis?
cards.back: Higher overall yield with less waste.
accept: Higher overall yield with less waste.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is high atom economy useful for green synthesis?
cards.back: More reactant atoms enter the desired product.
accept: More reactant atoms enter the desired product.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What splitting pattern does one adjacent equivalent proton cause?
cards.back: Doublet.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What splitting pattern do two adjacent equivalent protons cause?
cards.back: Triplet.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does a 3:2:1 NMR integration ratio represent?
cards.back: Three distinct environments containing three, two and one equivalent H.
accept: Three distinct environments containing three, two and one equivalent H.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does a counterexample establish?
cards.back: A universal statement is false.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What makes a function one-to-one?
cards.back: Different inputs give different outputs.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What must be true before a function has an inverse over its domain?
cards.back: It is one-to-one.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: In radians, what is arc length in a circle?
cards.back: s = rθ.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: On an E-alkene, where are the two higher-priority substituents?
cards.back: On opposite sides of the C=C bond.
accept: opposite sides of the double bond

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How many adjacent equivalent H atoms normally give a quartet in ¹H NMR?
cards.back: Three.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How can a force field be identified?
cards.back: A region where a body experiences a non-contact force.
accept: A region where a body experiences a non-contact force.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can an electric field repel but gravity cannot?
cards.back: Electric charges have both signs; gravitational mass is positive.
accept: Electric charges have both signs; gravitational mass is positive.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the difference between a scalar and vector field?
cards.back: A vector field has magnitude and direction at each point.
accept: A vector field has magnitude and direction at each point.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does gravitational force vary with separation of two point masses?
cards.back: Inversely with the square of distance.
accept: Inversely with the square of distance.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to gravitational field strength if radius from a point mass doubles?
cards.back: It becomes one quarter.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What do closely spaced gravitational field lines show?
cards.back: A stronger gravitational field.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does gravitational field strength equal in terms of force and mass?
cards.back: Force divided by mass, g = F/m.
accept: Force divided by mass, g = F/m.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the shape of a gravitational equipotential around an isolated spherical mass?
cards.back: Concentric spherical surfaces.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why is there no work along a gravitational equipotential?
cards.back: Gravitational potential does not change.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does gravitational potential vary with distance from a point mass?
cards.back: It equals −GM/r.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Which graph gives change in gravitational potential from its area?
cards.back: A graph of field strength against radial distance.
accept: A graph of field strength against radial distance.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is Kepler's third-law relationship for circular orbits?
cards.back: T² is proportional to r³.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What changes to orbital speed at larger circular orbital radius about one mass?
cards.back: It decreases.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why does a satellite in circular orbit accelerate despite constant speed?
cards.back: Its velocity continually changes direction.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What must be true of a geostationary satellite's angular speed?
cards.back: It equals Earth's rotational angular speed.
accept: It equals Earth's rotational angular speed.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does escape speed mean?
cards.back: Minimum speed to escape a body's gravitational field without further propulsion.
accept: Minimum speed to escape a body's gravitational field without further propulsion.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to electric force between point charges if separation triples?
cards.back: Its magnitude becomes one ninth.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How is electric field strength defined?
cards.back: Force per unit positive test charge.
accept: Force per unit positive test charge.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the electric field direction between parallel plates?
cards.back: From the positive plate to the negative plate.
accept: From the positive plate to the negative plate.
from positive plate to negative plate
from the positive plate to the negative plate
reject: from negative plate to positive plate
from the negative plate to the positive plate

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How is electric field strength related to uniform plate p.d. and separation?
cards.back: E = V/d.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What work is done when a charge Q crosses potential difference ΔV?
cards.back: ΔW = QΔV.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What shape are electric equipotentials around a point charge?
cards.back: Concentric spheres centred on the charge.
accept: Concentric spheres centred on the charge.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why is no electrical work done moving a charge along an equipotential?
cards.back: Its potential difference is zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: In which direction is the electric force on an electron relative to E?
cards.back: Opposite the electric field.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Which quantity is the slope of potential against distance related to?
cards.back: The electric field strength.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the sign of electric potential near an isolated negative charge?
cards.back: Negative.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can an electric field make a charged particle follow a curved path?
cards.back: Its force accelerates the particle sideways.
accept: Its force accelerates the particle sideways.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does parallel-plate capacitance change if plate separation halves?
cards.back: It doubles.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does parallel-plate capacitance change if plate area doubles?
cards.back: It doubles.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does a dielectric do to a capacitor's capacitance?
cards.back: It increases it.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can a polar dielectric increase capacitance?
cards.back: Molecular alignment reduces the effective electric field for a given free charge.
accept: Molecular alignment reduces the effective electric field for a given free charge.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the area under a p.d.–charge graph represent for a capacitor?
cards.back: Energy stored.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the energy stored by a capacitor in terms of C and V?
cards.back: E = ½CV².

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What fraction of final charge has accumulated after one RC charging time constant?
cards.back: About 63%.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the capacitor-discharge half-life expressed using RC?
cards.back: About 0.69RC.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux?
cards.back: Weber (Wb).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is magnetic flux through area A when the field is normal to it?
cards.back: Φ = BA.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: When is flux through a flat coil greatest in a uniform magnetic field?
cards.back: When the field is perpendicular to its plane.
accept: When the field is perpendicular to its plane.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does flux linkage represent?
cards.back: Magnetic flux times number of turns.
accept: Magnetic flux times number of turns.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: State the essence of Faraday's law.
cards.back: Induced emf is proportional to rate of change of flux linkage.
accept: Induced emf is proportional to rate of change of flux linkage.
rate of change of flux linkage

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the negative sign in Faraday's law represent?
cards.back: Lenz's law: the induced effect opposes the change causing it.
accept: Lenz's law: the induced effect opposes the change causing it.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the SI unit of induced emf?
cards.back: Volt (V).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What factor increases emf when a conductor cuts magnetic field lines faster?
cards.back: The rate of change of flux linkage rises.
accept: The rate of change of flux linkage rises.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does Fleming's left-hand first finger represent?
cards.back: Magnetic field direction.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does Fleming's left-hand thumb represent?
cards.back: Force or motion direction.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What do induced eddy currents circulate within?
cards.back: Bulk conducting material.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why are high voltages used for long-distance electrical transmission?
cards.back: Lower current reduces I²R power losses.
accept: Lower current reduces I²R power losses.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the peak-to-peak voltage of a sinusoid in terms of peak voltage?
cards.back: Twice the peak voltage.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does rms current quantify for an AC resistor?
cards.back: The DC current producing the same mean heating power.
accept: The DC current producing the same mean heating power.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What waveform does a uniformly rotating coil generate in a constant magnetic field?
cards.back: A sinusoidal induced emf.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What observation from alpha scattering showed atoms are mostly empty space?
cards.back: Most alpha particles passed straight through thin gold foil.
accept: Most alpha particles passed straight through thin gold foil.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What scattering observation showed a concentrated positive nucleus?
cards.back: A few alpha particles underwent very large deflections.
accept: A few alpha particles underwent very large deflections.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why could Rutherford not explain a stable atom using only orbiting classical electrons?
cards.back: Accelerating electrons should radiate energy and spiral inward.
accept: Accelerating electrons should radiate energy and spiral inward.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Which radiation is stopped most easily by thin paper?
cards.back: Alpha particles.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Which type of common nuclear radiation has no charge and no rest mass?
cards.back: Gamma radiation.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does gamma intensity change when distance from a point source doubles?
cards.back: Approximately one quarter.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why is background radiation subtracted from a sample's count rate?
cards.back: To estimate count rate due only to the source.
accept: To estimate count rate due only to the source.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does an alpha emission change nucleon number?
cards.back: It decreases by four.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does beta-minus emission change proton number?
cards.back: It increases by one.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the change in proton number during gamma emission?
cards.back: No change.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to a nucleus in gamma emission?
cards.back: It loses excitation energy.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does a nuclear chart of N against Z compare?
cards.back: Neutron number and proton number.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the approximate dependence of nuclear radius on nucleon number A?
cards.back: r is proportional to A^(1/3).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why is nuclear density approximately independent of nucleon number?
cards.back: Nuclear mass and volume both scale with A.
accept: Nuclear mass and volume both scale with A.
mass and volume scale with A

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How is binding energy defined for a nucleus?
cards.back: Energy required to separate it into free nucleons.
accept: Energy required to separate it into free nucleons.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the meaning of mass defect?
cards.back: Difference between free nucleon mass and bound nuclear mass.
accept: Difference between free nucleon mass and bound nuclear mass.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can fusion of light nuclei release energy?
cards.back: Products have greater binding energy per nucleon.
accept: Products have greater binding energy per nucleon.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What shape best describes radioactive count decay versus time?
cards.back: An exponential decrease.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the relation between half-life and decay constant?
cards.back: t½ = ln2/λ.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does an α detector's count vary with if distance increases?
cards.back: Count rate falls as fewer particles reach the detector.
accept: Count rate falls as fewer particles reach the detector.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which Group 2 metal is least reactive with cold water among Mg–Ba?
cards.back: Magnesium.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does Group 2 reactivity generally increase down the group?
cards.back: The outer electrons are removed more easily.
accept: The outer electrons are removed more easily.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does first ionisation energy fall down Group 2?
cards.back: Greater shielding and larger distance from the nucleus.
accept: Greater shielding and larger distance from the nucleus.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which Group 2 sulfate is very insoluble and used in contrast imaging?
cards.back: Barium sulfate.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the purpose of acidifying barium chloride in a sulfate test?
cards.back: To remove carbonate interference.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What observation suggests sulfate in an acidified barium-ion test?
cards.back: White barium sulfate precipitate.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which Group 2 hydroxide is used to reduce soil acidity?
cards.back: Calcium hydroxide.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What material is used to remove sulfur dioxide from flue gases?
cards.back: Calcium oxide or calcium carbonate.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which Group 2 metal helps reduce titanium tetrachloride to titanium?
cards.back: Magnesium.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What type of bonding is found in Group 2 elemental metals?
cards.back: Metallic bonding.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens to atomic radius down Group 2?
cards.back: It increases.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How does oxidising ability of halogens change down Group 7?
cards.back: It decreases.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How does reducing ability of halide ions change down Group 7?
cards.back: It increases.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why are fluorine and chlorine stronger oxidising agents than iodine?
cards.back: They gain electrons more readily.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does halogen electronegativity decrease down the group?
cards.back: Bonding electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded.
accept: Bonding electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which halogen displaces bromide and iodide from aqueous solutions?
cards.back: Chlorine.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which halogen displaces iodide but not chloride from aqueous solutions?
cards.back: Bromine.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Can iodine oxidise aqueous bromide to bromine under standard displacement conditions?
cards.back: No.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What observation indicates chloride in the silver-ion halide test?
cards.back: White precipitate.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What observation indicates bromide in the silver-ion halide test?
cards.back: Cream precipitate.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What observation indicates iodide in the silver-ion halide test?
cards.back: Yellow precipitate.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which silver halide requires concentrated ammonia to dissolve?
cards.back: Silver bromide.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which common silver halide does not dissolve even in concentrated ammonia?
cards.back: Silver iodide.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is the silver-ion halide test acidified with nitric acid?
cards.back: To remove interfering carbonate ions without adding chloride.
accept: To remove interfering carbonate ions without adding chloride.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What role does hypochlorous acid play in chlorinated drinking water?
cards.back: It acts as a disinfectant.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What term describes chlorine being both oxidised and reduced in one reaction?
cards.back: Disproportionation.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which reagent distinguishes AgCl and AgBr precipitates by solubility?
cards.back: Ammonia solution.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What trend do the colours of halogens show down Group 7?
cards.back: They become darker.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the oxidation state of chlorine in ClO⁻?

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which Period 3 oxide has a giant covalent structure?
cards.back: Silicon dioxide.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which oxide of Period 3 is amphoteric?
cards.back: Aluminium oxide.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which Period 3 oxides produce alkaline solutions in water?
cards.back: Sodium oxide and magnesium oxide.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does aluminium oxide react with both acids and alkalis?
cards.back: It is amphoteric.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What type of oxide is phosphorus(V) oxide?
cards.back: Acidic oxide.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What trend in oxide character occurs across Period 3?
cards.back: From basic through amphoteric to acidic.
accept: From basic through amphoteric to acidic.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is a ligand in coordination chemistry?
cards.back: A species that donates a lone pair to a metal ion.
accept: A species that donates a lone pair to a metal ion.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How many coordinate bonds does a hexadentate ligand form?
cards.back: Six.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is a chelate complex?
cards.back: A complex containing at least one multidentate ligand bonded at multiple sites.
accept: A complex containing at least one multidentate ligand bonded at multiple sites.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is a chelate often more stable than related monodentate complexes?
cards.back: Formation increases entropy by releasing more separate particles.
accept: Formation increases entropy by releasing more separate particles.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What changes colour when a ligand substitutes in a transition-metal complex?
cards.back: The d-orbital energy splitting changes.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which orbital subshell makes transition metals distinct in coordination chemistry?
cards.back: The d subshell.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the coordination number in a square planar complex such as [PtCl₄]²⁻?
cards.back: Four.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What colour is the common aqueous copper(II) hexaaqua complex?
cards.back: Pale blue.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What colour can the tetrahedral tetrachlorocuprate(II) complex appear?
cards.back: Yellow or greenish yellow.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the oxidation number of Fe in [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻?

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What do curly arrows show in an ionic organic mechanism?
cards.back: Movement of an electron pair.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Where must a curly arrow for new-bond formation start?
cards.back: At a bond or lone pair supplying the electrons.
accept: At a bond or lone pair supplying the electrons.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why must each carbon of C=C have two different groups for E/Z isomerism?
cards.back: Otherwise exchanging sides gives an identical arrangement.
accept: Otherwise exchanging sides gives an identical arrangement.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is a functional-group isomer?
cards.back: Same molecular formula but different functional groups.
accept: Same molecular formula but different functional groups.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the IR absorption range typically associated with an O–H alcohol bond?
cards.back: About 3230–3550 cm⁻¹.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What IR feature is characteristic of a carboxylic acid O–H?
cards.back: Very broad absorption around 2500–3300 cm⁻¹.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the fingerprint region of an IR spectrum typically below?

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which mass-spectrometry peak indicates the most abundant detected ion?
cards.back: The base peak.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is m/z measured as in ordinary mass spectra?
cards.back: Mass-to-charge ratio.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the structural group joining two carbonyls in an acid anhydride?
cards.back: An oxygen atom.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the characteristic smell of many small esters?
cards.back: Fruity.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can acid-catalysed ester formation have less than 100% conversion?
cards.back: It is reversible and reaches equilibrium.
accept: It is reversible and reaches equilibrium.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why are acyl chlorides generally more reactive than carboxylic acids?
cards.back: The carbonyl carbon is more susceptible to nucleophilic attack.
accept: The carbonyl carbon is more susceptible to nucleophilic attack.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What product class forms from reaction of an acyl chloride with an alcohol?
cards.back: An ester.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Where is the centre of mass of a uniform, regular solid?
cards.back: At its geometric centre.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For free fall from rest, where should a graph of s against t² ideally intercept?
cards.back: At the origin.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: In a free-fall s against t² graph, what can a non-zero intercept indicate?
cards.back: A systematic measurement offset.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Do melting points fall steadily from magnesium to barium?
cards.back: No. Calcium melts above magnesium; values then fall towards barium.
accept: No. Calcium melts above magnesium; values then fall towards barium.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does the melting point generally decrease from Ca to Ba?
cards.back: Larger metal ions lead to weaker metallic attraction.
accept: Larger metal ions lead to weaker metallic attraction.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Each burette reading is ±0.05 cm³. What is the titre's absolute uncertainty?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a small-angle pendulum, what is the gradient of T² against length?
cards.back: 4π²/g.
accept: four pi squared divided by g

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How can g be obtained from a graph of pendulum T² against length?
cards.back: g = 4π² ÷ gradient.
accept: four pi squared divided by gradient

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For N independent radioactive counts, what is the approximate count uncertainty?
cards.back: √N counts.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the approximate percentage uncertainty in N radioactive counts?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why does increasing the radioactive counting interval improve precision?
cards.back: More counts reduce the fractional counting uncertainty.
accept: More counts reduce the fractional counting uncertainty.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: At equivalence, what is the pH range for weak acid–strong base titration at 25°C?
cards.back: Above 7.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: At equivalence, what is the pH range for strong acid–weak base titration at 25°C?
cards.back: Below 7.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why do bonds absorb characteristic frequencies of infrared radiation?
cards.back: Different bond vibrations have different energy gaps.
accept: Different bond vibrations have different energy gaps.
reject: all bonds absorb the same frequency

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can CO₂ and methane contribute to global warming?
cards.back: They absorb and re-emit infrared radiation from Earth.
accept: They absorb and re-emit infrared radiation from Earth.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which DNA base bonds to platinum in cisplatin's action?
cards.back: Guanine.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can cisplatin have adverse effects on healthy cells?
cards.back: It may also interfere with DNA replication in healthy cells.
accept: It may also interfere with DNA replication in healthy cells.
affects DNA replication in healthy cells

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does adding mass spectrometry to gas chromatography help identify?
cards.back: Mass spectra of the separated components.
accept: Mass spectra of the separated components.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is gas-chromatography retention time alone not proof of identity?
cards.back: Different substances can have the same or similar retention time.
accept: Different substances can have the same or similar retention time.
different substances can have similar retention times
reject: every compound has a unique retention time

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How should a receiving aerial align to a linearly polarised radio wave?
cards.back: Parallel to the wave's electric-field oscillations.
accept: Parallel to the wave's electric-field oscillations.
reject: at right angles to E field

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to ideal light transmission through two crossed polarisers?
cards.back: No light is transmitted.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does a narrower single slit change its central diffraction maximum?
cards.back: The central maximum becomes wider.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: At fixed slit width, what increases the angular spread of diffraction?
cards.back: Increasing the wavelength.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the gravitational potential energy of a satellite of mass m at radius r?
cards.back: −GMm/r.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the kinetic energy of a satellite in a circular orbit of radius r?
cards.back: GMm/(2r).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the total orbital energy of a satellite in a circular orbit?
cards.back: −GMm/(2r).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why does raising a satellite to a larger circular orbit require energy?
cards.back: Its total orbital energy becomes less negative.
accept: Its total orbital energy becomes less negative.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is a TLC baseline generally marked in pencil rather than ink?
cards.back: Pencil graphite does not dissolve in the solvent like ink may.
accept: Pencil graphite does not dissolve in the solvent like ink may.
pencil does not dissolve in solvent

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Do chemically equivalent protons usually split each other's ¹H NMR signals?
cards.back: No; splitting comes from adjacent non-equivalent protons.
accept: No; splitting comes from adjacent non-equivalent protons.
equivalent protons do not split one another

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens to a proton's chemical shift if it is more shielded?
cards.back: Its chemical shift decreases (moves upfield).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why are ordinary carbon-13 NMR spectra typically less complex than ¹H spectra?
cards.back: Signals are usually recorded without proton-coupling splitting.
accept: Signals are usually recorded without proton-coupling splitting.
reject: more peaks due to proton splitting

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why may a solvent-free synthetic route produce less waste?
cards.back: There is no reaction solvent to dispose of or recover.
accept: There is no reaction solvent to dispose of or recover.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why are non-hazardous starting materials preferred in green chemistry?
cards.back: They reduce risks to people and the environment.
accept: They reduce risks to people and the environment.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the quadratic formula for ax² + bx + c = 0?

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the index law a^m × a^n.
cards.back: a^(m+n), for the same non-zero base.
accept: a^(m+n), for the same non-zero base.
a^, for the same non-zero base.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the index law (a^m)^n.
cards.back: a^(mn).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is logₐ1?
cards.back: 0, since a⁰ = 1 (a > 0, a ≠ 1).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is logₐa?
cards.back: 1, for a > 0 and a ≠ 1.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the point–gradient form of a straight-line equation.
cards.back: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the sum of n terms of an arithmetic progression?

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the sum of n terms of a geometric progression?
cards.back: Sₙ = a(1−rⁿ)/(1−r), when r ≠ 1.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the sum to infinity for a convergent geometric series?
cards.back: S∞ = a/(1−r), valid when |r| < 1.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the radian sector-area formula?
cards.back: A = ½r²θ, with θ in radians.
accept: A = ½r²θ, with θ in radians.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the identity linking sec²x and tan²x.
cards.back: sec²x = 1 + tan²x.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the identity linking cosec²x and cot²x.
cards.back: cosec²x = 1 + cot²x.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is sin 2x in terms of sin x and cos x?
cards.back: sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is cos 2x in terms of cos²x and sin²x?
cards.back: cos 2x = cos²x − sin²x.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is tan 2x in terms of tan x?
cards.back: tan 2x = 2 tan x/(1−tan²x), where defined.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is d(sin kx)/dx?
cards.back: k cos(kx), using radians.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is d(cos kx)/dx?
cards.back: −k sin(kx), using radians.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is d(e^(kx))/dx?
cards.back: k e^(kx).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is d(ln x)/dx?
cards.back: 1/x (for x > 0).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the product rule for y = uv.
cards.back: dy/dx = u′v + uv′.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the quotient rule for y = u/v.
cards.back: dy/dx = (vu′ − uv′)/v².

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the chain rule for y = f(g(x)).
cards.back: dy/dx = f′(g(x))g′(x).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is ∫e^(kx) dx, for k ≠ 0?
cards.back: e^(kx)/k + C.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is ∫1/x dx?
cards.back: ln|x| + C (on a suitable interval).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is ∫sin(kx) dx for k ≠ 0?
cards.back: −cos(kx)/k + C.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is ∫cos(kx) dx for k ≠ 0?
cards.back: sin(kx)/k + C.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State integration by parts in its standard form.
cards.back: ∫u(dv/dx) dx = uv − ∫v(du/dx) dx.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: How is a value standardised for X ~ N(μ,σ²)?
cards.back: z = (x−μ)/σ.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: For X~B(n,p), what are E(X) and Var(X)?
cards.back: E(X) = np; Var(X) = np(1−p).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is a one-sided hypothesis test looking for?
cards.back: Evidence of a difference in one specified direction.
accept: Evidence of a difference in one specified direction.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: In variable-acceleration motion, how is v related to displacement s?
cards.back: v = ds/dt.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: In variable-acceleration motion, how is a related to v?
cards.back: a = dv/dt.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a product or quotient, how do percentage uncertainties combine?
cards.back: Add percentage uncertainties (usual worst-case estimate).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How can uncertainty in a fitted line's y-intercept be estimated?
cards.back: Compare best-fit with extreme acceptable line intercepts.
accept: Compare best-fit with extreme acceptable line intercepts.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What two conservation laws must hold in pair production?
cards.back: Energy and momentum are both conserved.
accept: Energy and momentum are both conserved.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can't a single photon create a pair in empty space?
cards.back: A lone photon cannot conserve both energy and momentum.
accept: A lone photon cannot conserve both energy and momentum.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the strangeness of an s quark?
cards.back: −1 (an anti-s has +1).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the distinction between amplitude and peak-to-peak displacement?
cards.back: Peak-to-peak displacement is twice the amplitude.
accept: Peak-to-peak displacement is twice the amplitude.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: When are two superposed waves exactly in antiphase?
cards.back: They have a phase difference of 180° or π radians.
accept: They have a phase difference of 180° or π radians.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a Hooke's-law spring, how is stored strain energy found?
cards.back: E = ½Fx = ½kx², from the force–extension graph area.
accept: E = ½Fx = ½kx², from the force–extension graph area.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What defines the critical temperature of a superconductor?
cards.back: At or below it the material's resistivity is zero.
accept: At or below it the material's resistivity is zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What changes in an emf–terminal-voltage graph as current rises?
cards.back: Lost volts Ir increases; terminal p.d. decreases.
accept: Lost volts Ir increases; terminal p.d. decreases.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the acceleration at the equilibrium position in SHM?
cards.back: Zero, because displacement x = 0.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: In the gas equation pV = NkT, what does N count?
cards.back: The number of gas molecules, not moles.
accept: The number of gas molecules, not moles.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why is rms speed not the same as mean speed?
cards.back: Rms uses the square root of the mean squared speed.
accept: Rms uses the square root of the mean squared speed.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does an equipotential surface tell you about work along it?
cards.back: No work is done by the electric field moving charge along it.
accept: No work is done by the electric field moving charge along it.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why convert cm³ to dm³ when calculating molar concentration?
cards.back: Concentration in mol dm⁻³ uses volume in dm³; divide cm³ by 1000.
accept: Concentration in mol dm⁻³ uses volume in dm³; divide cm³ by 1000.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the difference between a bond pair and a lone pair?
cards.back: A bond pair is shared between atoms; a lone pair is not.
accept: A bond pair is shared between atoms; a lone pair is not.
A bond pair is shared between atoms

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In calorimetry, why may the calculated |ΔH| be too small?
cards.back: Heat loss to surroundings makes measured |ΔT| too small.
accept: Heat loss to surroundings makes measured |ΔT| too small.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens to Kc if concentrations change but temperature stays constant?
cards.back: It stays the same; the position may shift.
accept: It stays the same; the position may shift.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why do we weigh both benefits and risks of water chlorination?
cards.back: It prevents infections, but toxic chlorine or by-products require control.
accept: It prevents infections, but toxic chlorine or by-products require control.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the role of the nucleophile in nucleophilic substitution?
cards.back: It donates an electron pair to the electrophilic carbon.
accept: It donates an electron pair to the electrophilic carbon.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What distinguishes an addition polymer from its monomer?
cards.back: The monomer's C=C bonds open to form a saturated chain.
accept: The monomer's C=C bonds open to form a saturated chain.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What distinguishes oxidation of primary and secondary alcohols?
cards.back: Primary can form aldehyde/acid; secondary forms ketone.
accept: Primary can form aldehyde/acid; secondary forms ketone.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does a positive 2,4-DNPH test usually indicate?
cards.back: An aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group.
accept: An aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is ΔG in terms of ΔH and ΔS?
cards.back: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, with consistent units.
accept: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, with consistent units.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What quantity, not concentration, is used in a Kp expression?
cards.back: Equilibrium partial pressure of each gas.
accept: Equilibrium partial pressure of each gas.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the pKa definition?
cards.back: pKa = −log₁₀(Ka).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How is [H⁺] found from a pH value?
cards.back: [H⁺] = 10^(−pH) mol dm⁻³.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How does an acidic buffer resist small pH changes?
cards.back: HA removes added OH⁻; A⁻ removes added H⁺.
accept: HA removes added OH⁻; A⁻ removes added H⁺.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why do transition-metal complex ions often have colour?
cards.back: Ligand-field splitting allows absorption of visible wavelengths.
accept: Ligand-field splitting allows absorption of visible wavelengths.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does a zero discriminant tell you about a quadratic?
cards.back: It has one repeated real root.
accept: It has one repeated real root.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: How is the domain of f⁻¹ related to f?
cards.back: It is the range of f.
accept: It is the range of f.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: How is the range of f⁻¹ related to f?
cards.back: It is the domain of f.
accept: It is the domain of f.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does a remainder of zero show about a polynomial divisor (x−a)?
cards.back: (x−a) is a factor of the polynomial.
accept: (x−a) is a factor of the polynomial.
is a factor of the polynomial.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does Σ from r=1 to n mean?
cards.back: Add the listed expression for r = 1, 2, …, n.
accept: Add the listed expression for r = 1, 2, …, n.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: For a geometric sum, what happens when r=1?
cards.back: All n terms equal a, so Sₙ = na.
accept: All n terms equal a, so Sₙ = na.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What are the exact values of sin(π/6) and cos(π/3)?
cards.back: Both equal 1/2.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What are the exact values of sin(π/4) and cos(π/4)?
cards.back: Both equal √2/2.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does f′(a)=0 tell you about a smooth curve?
cards.back: It has a stationary point at x=a.
accept: It has a stationary point at x=a.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: Why is the constant of integration needed in an indefinite integral?
cards.back: All antiderivatives differ by a constant.
accept: All antiderivatives differ by a constant.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: If u = g(x), what is du in integration by substitution?
cards.back: du = g′(x) dx.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: When does a sign change bracket a root?
cards.back: If f is continuous and f(a)f(b)<0, at least one root lies between.
accept: If f is continuous and f(a)f(b)<0, at least one root lies between.
If f is continuous and ff<0, at least one root lies between.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the difference between a test statistic and a p-value?
cards.back: Statistic summarises data; p-value measures extremeness under H₀.
accept: Statistic summarises data; p-value measures extremeness under H₀.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What conditions establish equilibrium of a rigid body in a plane?
cards.back: Resultant force zero and resultant moment zero.
accept: Resultant force zero and resultant moment zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is resolution of a digital measuring instrument?
cards.back: The smallest displayed change in the reading.
accept: The smallest displayed change in the reading.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What must happen to both momentum and energy in annihilation?
cards.back: Both must be conserved.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What distinguishes strong from weak interactions in a strangeness-changing decay?
cards.back: Strangeness can change in weak interactions, not strong interactions.
accept: Strangeness can change in weak interactions, not strong interactions.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can below-threshold light not eject electrons by increasing intensity?
cards.back: Each photon has insufficient energy to overcome the work function.
accept: Each photon has insufficient energy to overcome the work function.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How much is one complete oscillation in radians of phase?
cards.back: 2π radians.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does a phase difference of π/2 represent?
cards.back: One-quarter of a cycle (90°).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: In double-slit interference, what is the path difference at the centre?
cards.back: Zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does a negative velocity mean on a signed motion graph?
cards.back: Motion in the negative chosen direction.
accept: Motion in the negative chosen direction.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can displacement be zero when distance travelled is not?
cards.back: Opposite-direction displacements can cancel.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why does a filament lamp show increasing resistance as voltage rises?
cards.back: The filament gets hotter and its resistance rises.
accept: The filament gets hotter and its resistance rises.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why does a diode have negligible reverse current normally?
cards.back: It strongly resists conduction under reverse bias.
accept: It strongly resists conduction under reverse bias.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the phase difference between SHM displacement and acceleration?
cards.back: π radians (180°), since a = −ω²x.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a monatomic ideal gas, how is U related to T?
cards.back: U = 3/2 nRT.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Which way does the induced current act relative to a flux change?
cards.back: It opposes the change that produced it (Lenz's law).
accept: It opposes the change that produced it (Lenz's law).
It opposes the change that produced it.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the shape of a graph of ln(activity) against time?
cards.back: A straight line with gradient −λ.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In a back titration, what does the measured leftover reagent determine?
cards.back: How much excess reagent remained after the first reaction.
accept: How much excess reagent remained after the first reaction.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How does an extra lone pair typically affect the bond angle?
cards.back: It reduces the bond angle through stronger repulsion.
accept: It reduces the bond angle through stronger repulsion.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which feature of a Maxwell–Boltzmann curve gives the fraction above Eₐ?
cards.back: The area under the curve to the right of Eₐ.
accept: The area under the curve to the right of Eₐ.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: For an exothermic equilibrium, how does increasing T affect Kc?
cards.back: Kc decreases.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is barium sulfate suitable as an insoluble contrast compound?
cards.back: It is very insoluble, limiting release of barium ions.
accept: It is very insoluble, limiting release of barium ions.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Where must a full curly arrow start in an organic mechanism?
cards.back: At a lone pair or covalent bond containing the moving electron pair.
accept: At a lone pair or covalent bond containing the moving electron pair.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What type of reaction converts an alkene into an alkane?
cards.back: Addition of hydrogen (hydrogenation).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why must an aldehyde be distilled off during primary-alcohol oxidation?
cards.back: To limit further oxidation to a carboxylic acid.
accept: To limit further oxidation to a carboxylic acid.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: When can an endothermic reaction be feasible from ΔG?
cards.back: When TΔS exceeds ΔH, making ΔG < 0.
accept: When TΔS exceeds ΔH, making ΔG < 0.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens to rate if [A] doubles in a first-order reaction?
cards.back: Rate doubles, with other factors unchanged.
accept: Rate doubles, with other factors unchanged.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens to rate if [A] doubles in a second-order reaction?
cards.back: Rate becomes four times larger, all else constant.
accept: Rate becomes four times larger, all else constant.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: When pressure changes at constant temperature, does Kp change?
cards.back: No; Kp depends only on temperature.
accept: No; Kp depends only on temperature.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How does a pH meter differ from an indicator at equivalence?
cards.back: It measures the full pH change rather than only a colour transition.
accept: It measures the full pH change rather than only a colour transition.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can two complexes of the same metal ion have different colours?
cards.back: Different ligands change d-orbital splitting and absorbed wavelengths.
accept: Different ligands change d-orbital splitting and absorbed wavelengths.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is TMS a useful chemical-shift reference?
cards.back: It produces a single signal defined as δ = 0 ppm.
accept: It produces a single signal defined as δ = 0 ppm.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the logarithm quotient law for logₐ(x/y).
cards.back: logₐ(x/y) = logₐx − logₐy (x,y>0; a>0, a≠1).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What are the relative charges of proton, neutron and electron?
cards.back: Proton +1; neutron 0; electron −1.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What are the approximate relative masses of proton, neutron and electron?
cards.back: About 1, 1 and 1/1836, respectively.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How do the resistances of series-connected components combine?
cards.back: Rₜ = R₁ + R₂ + … .

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the rule for equivalent resistance of two parallel resistors?
cards.back: 1/Rₜ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to Vout across an NTC thermistor as temperature increases?
cards.back: Vout falls when supply voltage and the other series resistance are fixed.
accept: Vout falls when supply voltage and the other series resistance are fixed.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to Vout across the fixed resistor as an NTC warms?
cards.back: Vout rises because the thermistor resistance falls.
accept: Vout rises because the thermistor resistance falls.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to Vout across an LDR in brighter light?
cards.back: Vout falls for fixed supply voltage and other series resistance.
accept: Vout falls for fixed supply voltage and other series resistance.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For an ohmic V–I graph (V vertical), what is its gradient?
cards.back: Resistance R.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For an ohmic I–V graph (I vertical), what is its gradient?
cards.back: Conductance 1/R.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does saturated mean for an alkane?
cards.back: No carbon–carbon multiple bonds; only C–C single bonds.
accept: No carbon–carbon multiple bonds; only C–C single bonds.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How is the unpaired electron of a radical drawn?
cards.back: With a single dot, e.g. Cl•.
accept: With a single dot, e.g. Cl•.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Are full curly electron-pair arrows needed for radical substitution?
cards.back: No. Radical mechanisms are shown without electron-pair curly arrows.
accept: No. Radical mechanisms are shown without electron-pair curly arrows.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: If a TLC spot stays put but the solvent front travels further, what happens to Rf?
cards.back: Rf decreases: the solvent-front distance in the denominator increases.
accept: Rf decreases: the solvent-front distance in the denominator increases.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why must a TLC starting spot be above the solvent level?
cards.back: So the sample travels up the plate rather than dissolving in the solvent pool.
accept: So the sample travels up the plate rather than dissolving in the solvent pool.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How do you find the number of neutrons from nuclide notation?
cards.back: N = A − Z, where A is nucleon number and Z is proton number.
accept: N = A − Z, where A is nucleon number and Z is proton number.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For two isotopes of one element, what stays the same and what differs?
cards.back: Same proton number Z; different neutron numbers and nucleon numbers A.
accept: Same proton number Z; different neutron numbers and nucleon numbers A.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What are the baryon numbers of baryons and antibaryons?
cards.back: Baryons +1; antibaryons −1.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the charge of a strange quark?
cards.back: −1/3 of the elementary charge.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Define resistivity ρ for a uniform conductor.
cards.back: A property of the material: ρ = RA/L at a given temperature; SI unit Ω m.
accept: A property of the material: ρ = RA/L at a given temperature; SI unit Ω m.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why does total current entering a junction equal current leaving?
cards.back: Charge is conserved; no net charge accumulates at the junction.
accept: Charge is conserved; no net charge accumulates at the junction.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why do potential differences around a complete circuit loop sum to zero?
cards.back: Energy is conserved: energy supplied per charge equals energy transferred per charge.
accept: Energy is conserved: energy supplied per charge equals energy transferred per charge.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What are approximate proton and electron masses in kilograms?
cards.back: Proton 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg; electron 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Define an alkane.
cards.back: A saturated hydrocarbon containing only carbon–carbon single bonds.
accept: A saturated hydrocarbon containing only carbon–carbon single bonds.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What carbon-containing products can form in incomplete hydrocarbon combustion?
cards.back: Carbon monoxide (CO) and solid carbon (soot); some CO₂ may also form.
accept: Carbon monoxide (CO) and solid carbon (soot); some CO₂ may also form.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What catalyst is associated with catalytic cracking and what products are valuable?
cards.back: A zeolite catalyst; valuable products include motor fuels and aromatic hydrocarbons.
accept: A zeolite catalyst; valuable products include motor fuels and aromatic hydrocarbons.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the economic reason for cracking long-chain alkane fractions?
cards.back: To convert less-demanded heavy fractions into more useful, higher-demand fuels and chemical feedstocks.
accept: To convert less-demanded heavy fractions into more useful, higher-demand fuels and chemical feedstocks.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How is a secondary amine classified by its nitrogen bonds?
cards.back: Nitrogen is bonded to two carbon-containing groups.
accept: Nitrogen is bonded to two carbon-containing groups.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How is a tertiary amine classified by its nitrogen bonds?
cards.back: Nitrogen is bonded to three carbon-containing groups.
accept: Nitrogen is bonded to three carbon-containing groups.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can incinerating polymer waste cause environmental problems?
cards.back: It releases CO₂ and may produce harmful gases if emissions are not controlled.
accept: It releases CO₂ and may produce harmful gases if emissions are not controlled.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can recycling mixed polymer waste be difficult?
cards.back: Different polymers have different properties and may need sorting before reprocessing.
accept: Different polymers have different properties and may need sorting before reprocessing.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does one mole of specified particles represent?
cards.back: An amount containing the Avogadro number of particles (atoms, ions, molecules or other entities).
accept: An amount containing the Avogadro number of particles (atoms, ions, molecules or other entities).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Give the formulae and charges of phosphate and hydrogencarbonate ions.
cards.back: Phosphate PO₄³⁻; hydrogencarbonate HCO₃⁻.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What charge rule must the formula of an ionic compound satisfy?
cards.back: The total positive and negative ionic charges must cancel to give zero overall charge.
accept: The total positive and negative ionic charges must cancel to give zero overall charge.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can a solid metal conduct electricity?
cards.back: It contains mobile delocalised electrons that carry charge through the solid.
accept: It contains mobile delocalised electrons that carry charge through the solid.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why do simple molecular substances usually not conduct electricity?
cards.back: They have no freely moving ions or delocalised electrons to carry charge.
