accept: They have no freely moving ions or delocalised electrons to carry charge.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does the melting point generally rise from sodium to aluminium?
cards.back: Metallic bonds strengthen as ion charge and delocalised electrons increase and ion size falls.
accept: Metallic bonds strengthen as ion charge and delocalised electrons increase and ion size falls.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does sulfur have a higher melting point than chlorine?
cards.back: S₈ molecules are larger than Cl₂ and have more electrons, giving stronger induced dipole forces.
accept: S₈ molecules are larger than Cl₂ and have more electrons, giving stronger induced dipole forces.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does argon have a lower melting point than chlorine?
cards.back: Ar is monatomic, with fewer electrons and weaker induced dipole attractions than Cl₂.
accept: Ar is monatomic, with fewer electrons and weaker induced dipole attractions than Cl₂.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: On a capacitor charge–time graph, what does the tangent's gradient give?
cards.back: Instantaneous current, I = dQ/dt (including its sign).
accept: Instantaneous current, I = dQ/dt (including its sign).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the signed area under a current–time graph give?
cards.back: The charge transferred, ΔQ = ∫ I dt.
accept: The charge transferred, ΔQ = ∫ I dt.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the gradient of ln Q against time for capacitor discharge?
cards.back: −1/(RC), so the time constant is the reciprocal of the gradient's magnitude.
accept: −1/(RC), so the time constant is the reciprocal of the gradient's magnitude.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does the signed area under an electric field–distance graph represent?
cards.back: The negative potential change along that direction: ΔV = −∫ E dr.
accept: The negative potential change along that direction: ΔV = −∫ E dr.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the approximate size of an atomic nucleus?
cards.back: Its radius is of order 10⁻¹⁵ m (a few femtometres).
accept: Its radius is of order 10⁻¹⁵ m (a few femtometres).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: At an alpha particle's head-on closest approach, what has happened to its kinetic energy?
cards.back: It has become electrostatic potential energy, neglecting nuclear recoil.
accept: It has become electrostatic potential energy, neglecting nuclear recoil.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How can electron diffraction provide information about nuclear radius?
cards.back: The angles of diffraction minima depend on the size of the nucleus.
accept: The angles of diffraction minima depend on the size of the nucleus.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What energy is equivalent to a mass of 1 unified atomic mass unit?
cards.back: About 931.5 MeV.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the negative-electrode half-equation in the simplified lithium cell?
cards.back: Li → Li⁺ + e⁻.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the positive-electrode half-equation in AQA's simplified lithium cell?
cards.back: Li⁺ + CoO₂ + e⁻ → Li⁺[CoO₂]⁻.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the hydrogen-electrode half-equation in an alkaline fuel cell?
cards.back: H₂ + 2OH⁻ → 2H₂O + 2e⁻.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the oxygen-electrode half-equation in an alkaline fuel cell?
cards.back: O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the displayed structural formula of phosphoric acid?
cards.back: O=P(OH)₃ (equivalently H₃PO₄).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which ion forms when phosphoric acid loses its first proton?
cards.back: H₂PO₄⁻, the dihydrogen phosphate ion.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which ion forms on the first deprotonation of sulfurous acid?
cards.back: HSO₃⁻, the hydrogensulfite ion.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which ion forms on the first deprotonation of sulfuric acid?
cards.back: HSO₄⁻, the hydrogensulfate ion.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does silicon dioxide not react with water under ordinary conditions?
cards.back: Its strong giant covalent Si–O network is not readily broken by water.
accept: Its strong giant covalent Si–O network is not readily broken by water.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What colour is the aqueous vanadium(IV) species?
cards.back: Blue.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What colour is the aqueous vanadium(III) species?
cards.back: Green.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What colour is the aqueous vanadium(II) species?
cards.back: Purple (violet).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens to Fe²⁺ with aqueous ammonia, including excess ammonia?
cards.back: Green Fe(OH)₂ precipitates and remains insoluble in excess ammonia.
accept: Green Fe(OH)₂ precipitates and remains insoluble in excess ammonia.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How does the Al³⁺ hydroxide precipitate behave with excess ammonia versus excess hydroxide?
cards.back: It stays as a white solid in excess NH₃ but dissolves in excess OH⁻.
accept: It stays as a white solid in excess NH₃ but dissolves in excess OH⁻.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is usually observed when a 3+ hexaaqua ion reacts with carbonate?
cards.back: A metal hydroxide precipitate forms with bubbles of CO₂.
accept: A metal hydroxide precipitate forms with bubbles of CO₂.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: For an octahedral complex [MA₄B₂], how do cis and trans differ?
cards.back: Cis: B ligands adjacent (90°). Trans: B ligands opposite (180°).
accept: Cis: B ligands adjacent (90°). Trans: B ligands opposite (180°).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can a coloured complex appear a different colour from the light it absorbs?
cards.back: The observed colour comes from the visible wavelengths transmitted or reflected, not absorbed.
accept: The observed colour comes from the visible wavelengths transmitted or reflected, not absorbed.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does a positive E°cell not tell you how quickly a reaction occurs?
cards.back: It indicates thermodynamic tendency, not reaction rate or activation energy.
accept: It indicates thermodynamic tendency, not reaction rate or activation energy.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why might a cell's measured emf differ from its standard emf?
cards.back: Its temperature, concentrations or gas pressures may differ from standard conditions.
accept: Its temperature, concentrations or gas pressures may differ from standard conditions.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In a skeletal formula, what does each unlabelled line end represent?
cards.back: One carbon atom.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In a skeletal formula, how many bonds does neutral carbon normally make?
cards.back: Four covalent bonds, with omitted C–H bonds implied.
accept: Four covalent bonds, with omitted C–H bonds implied.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Fill the gap: an empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ___ of atoms.
cards.back: ratio

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Name CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃.
cards.back: 2-methylbutane.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Name CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃.
cards.back: Butan-2-ol.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: When naming an ester, which part of the name comes first?
cards.back: The alkyl part derived from the alcohol.
accept: The alkyl part derived from the alcohol.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How many carbons are in the parent chain named pent-?
cards.back: Five.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which atom counts as carbon 1 in a carboxylic acid?
cards.back: The carbon atom of the –COOH group.
accept: The carbon atom of the –COOH group.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: When a C–Br bond breaks heterolytically, where does its curly arrow point?
cards.back: Towards Br, which takes the bonding electron pair.
accept: Towards Br, which takes the bonding electron pair.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Choose the correct arrow source: A electrophile; B lone pair; C positive charge.
cards.back: B: the lone pair supplying the electrons.
accept: B: the lone pair supplying the electrons.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How is stereoisomerism different from structural isomerism?
cards.back: Same connectivity but a different arrangement in space.
accept: Same connectivity but a different arrangement in space.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In CIP ranking, if attached atoms tie, what do you compare next?
cards.back: Their attached atoms, ordered by atomic number, until the first difference.
accept: Their attached atoms, ordered by atomic number, until the first difference.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: CIP: which has higher priority, –CH₂OH or –CH₃?
cards.back: –CH₂OH: its next attached atoms include oxygen.
accept: –CH₂OH: its next attached atoms include oxygen.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is a crude-oil fraction?
cards.back: A mixture of hydrocarbons with similar boiling points.
accept: A mixture of hydrocarbons with similar boiling points.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Fill the gap: a fractionating column is cooler near the ___.
cards.back: top

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Where do higher-boiling crude-oil fractions condense?
cards.back: Lower down the hotter fractionating column.
accept: Lower down the hotter fractionating column.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Is fractional distillation a chemical change or physical separation?
cards.back: Physical separation; no hydrocarbon molecules are changed.
accept: Physical separation; no hydrocarbon molecules are changed.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why do larger alkane molecules generally have higher boiling points?
cards.back: More electrons produce stronger London dispersion forces.
accept: More electrons produce stronger London dispersion forces.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which cracking method uses high temperature and high pressure?
cards.back: Thermal cracking.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Fill the gap: catalytic cracking uses a ___ catalyst.
cards.back: zeolite

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can nitrogen oxides form inside combustion engines?
cards.back: High temperatures allow nitrogen and oxygen from air to react.
accept: High temperatures allow nitrogen and oxygen from air to react.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In a catalytic converter, CO is oxidised to which gas?
cards.back: Carbon dioxide, CO₂.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In a catalytic converter, nitrogen oxides are reduced to what?
cards.back: Nitrogen, N₂.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Complete the flue-gas equation: CaO + SO₂ → ___
cards.back: CaSO₃.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Complete the flue-gas equation: CaCO₃ + SO₂ → CaSO₃ + ___
cards.back: CO₂.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Radical initiation: fill the gap, Cl₂ → ___ (under UV).
cards.back: 2Cl•

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Radical propagation 1: Cl• + CH₄ → HCl + ___
cards.back: CH₃•

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Radical propagation 2: CH₃• + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + ___
cards.back: Cl•

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens next after CH₃• reacts with Cl₂ in propagation?
cards.back: A chlorine radical is regenerated and can continue the chain.
accept: A chlorine radical is regenerated and can continue the chain.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Termination: complete CH₃• + CH₃• → ___
cards.back: C₂H₆.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can methane chlorination give several chlorinated products?
cards.back: The products can undergo further radical substitution.
accept: The products can undergo further radical substitution.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In a radical mechanism, what does a dot after a symbol mean?
cards.back: An unpaired electron, not an ionic charge.
accept: An unpaired electron, not an ionic charge.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: A C–X carbon is bonded to two other carbons. Classify the halogenoalkane.
cards.back: Secondary.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Substitution arrow 1: OH⁻ attacks which atom of a halogenoalkane?
cards.back: The δ⁺ carbon bonded to the halogen.
accept: The δ⁺ carbon bonded to the halogen.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Substitution arrow 2: where does the C–Br bond's electron pair move?
cards.back: To bromine, which leaves as Br⁻.
accept: To bromine, which leaves as Br⁻.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In nucleophilic substitution by CN⁻, which end forms the C–C bond?
cards.back: The carbon end of CN⁻.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Fill the gap: substitution of R–Br with NH₃ first gives R–NH₃___.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens after the positively charged RNH₃⁺ intermediate forms?
cards.back: A base removes H⁺, giving a neutral primary amine.
accept: A base removes H⁺, giving a neutral primary amine.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In elimination by OH⁻, does OH⁻ attack carbon or an adjacent hydrogen?
cards.back: An adjacent (β) hydrogen; OH⁻ acts as a base.
accept: An adjacent (β) hydrogen; OH⁻ acts as a base.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Elimination arrow 1: where does the oxygen lone pair of OH⁻ point?
cards.back: To a hydrogen on the carbon next to the C–Br carbon.
accept: To a hydrogen on the carbon next to the C–Br carbon.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Elimination arrow 2: where do the β C–H bonding electrons move?
cards.back: Into the bond between the two carbons, forming C=C.
accept: Into the bond between the two carbons, forming C=C.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Elimination arrow 3: where do the C–Br bonding electrons move?
cards.back: To Br, forming Br⁻.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Elimination of 2-bromobutane: name two possible alkene position isomers.
cards.back: But-1-ene and but-2-ene.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Ozone cycle step 1: Cl• + O₃ → ClO• + ___
cards.back: O₂.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Ozone cycle step 2: ClO• + O₃ → Cl• + ___
cards.back: 2O₂.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is cancelled when the two chlorine-radical ozone steps are added?
cards.back: Cl• and ClO•, as both are regenerated or intermediates.
accept: Cl• and ClO•, as both are regenerated or intermediates.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Complete the net ozone-decomposition equation: 2O₃ → ___
cards.back: 3O₂.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How does AQA describe the bonding in an alkene?
cards.back: A C=C double covalent bond that is a centre of high electron density.
accept: A C=C double covalent bond that is a centre of high electron density.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What structural feature of C=C makes E/Z isomerism possible?
cards.back: Rotation around a C=C double bond is restricted.
accept: Rotation around a C=C double bond is restricted.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: HBr addition arrow 2: where does the H–Br bond's electron pair go?
cards.back: To bromine, forming Br⁻.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: After HBr protonates ethene, which charged intermediate forms?
cards.back: The ethyl carbocation, CH₃CH₂⁺.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: HBr addition final arrow: where does the Br⁻ lone pair point?
cards.back: Towards the positively charged carbon of the carbocation.
accept: Towards the positively charged carbon of the carbocation.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does Br₂ become polarised as it approaches an alkene?
cards.back: The electron-rich C=C bond repels Br₂ electrons, inducing a dipole.
accept: The electron-rich C=C bond repels Br₂ electrons, inducing a dipole.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the product of adding Br₂ to ethene?
cards.back: 1,2-dibromoethane.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the immediate product of ethene + H₂SO₄?
cards.back: Ethyl hydrogensulfate, CH₃CH₂OSO₃H.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: After H₂SO₄ protonates ethene, which ion attacks the carbocation?
cards.back: Hydrogensulfate, HSO₄⁻, through oxygen.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In the major product from propene + HBr, which carbon bears bromine?
cards.back: Carbon 2 (forming 2-bromopropane).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In a polymer repeating-unit diagram, where is n placed?
cards.back: Outside the square brackets.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What must pass through both ends of a polymer's repeating-unit brackets?
cards.back: The two continuation bonds.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Poly(propene) has which side group on its carbon backbone?
cards.back: A methyl (–CH₃) group.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the monomer of poly(chloroethene), PVC?
cards.back: Chloroethene, CH₂=CHCl.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the overall fermentation equation for glucose to ethanol?
cards.back: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the reaction type when ethene becomes ethanol with water?
cards.back: Hydration (addition).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which colour change shows Cr₂O₇²⁻ reducing to Cr³⁺ in alcohol oxidation?
cards.back: Orange to green.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which oxidation state does chromium change from/to in dichromate oxidation?

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why use distillation rather than reflux to isolate an aldehyde?
cards.back: Distillation removes the aldehyde before it can oxidise further.
accept: Distillation removes the aldehyde before it can oxidise further.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does reflux prevent loss of volatile reactants?
cards.back: Vapour condenses and returns to the reaction vessel.
accept: Vapour condenses and returns to the reaction vessel.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Alcohol dehydration mechanism step 1: what happens to the –OH group?
cards.back: It is protonated to –OH₂⁺, making water a better leaving group.
accept: It is protonated to –OH₂⁺, making water a better leaving group.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Alcohol dehydration: after protonation, what group can leave?
cards.back: Water, H₂O.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Alcohol dehydration: which proton is removed to form the C=C bond?
cards.back: A β-hydrogen on a carbon next to the former –OH carbon.
accept: A β-hydrogen on a carbon next to the former –OH carbon.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Alcohol dehydration: what happens to the acid catalyst overall?
cards.back: It is regenerated.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can dehydration of an unsymmetrical alcohol give different alkenes?
cards.back: A β-hydrogen can be removed from different adjacent carbons.
accept: A β-hydrogen can be removed from different adjacent carbons.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which test would show an aldehyde but not a typical simple ketone?
cards.back: Tollens' or Fehling's reagent gives a positive result.
accept: Tollens' or Fehling's reagent gives a positive result.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How can a high-resolution mass spectrum help find a molecular formula?
cards.back: Its precise molecular mass can distinguish elemental compositions.
accept: Its precise molecular mass can distinguish elemental compositions.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How does an IR spectrum help identify a functional group?
cards.back: Characteristic bonds absorb at characteristic wavenumbers.
accept: Characteristic bonds absorb at characteristic wavenumbers.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How can an IR spectrum help reveal an impurity?
cards.back: It may show additional absorption peaks absent from the pure compound.
accept: It may show additional absorption peaks absent from the pure compound.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Ammonia substitution: where does the next NH₃ lone-pair arrow point?
cards.back: Towards H on the positively charged RNH₃⁺ intermediate.
accept: Towards H on the positively charged RNH₃⁺ intermediate.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Ammonia deprotonation: where do the R–NH₃⁺ N–H bond electrons go?
cards.back: Back onto its nitrogen atom, giving the neutral amine.
accept: Back onto its nitrogen atom, giving the neutral amine.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: When CN⁻ replaces a halogen in R–X, how does the carbon count change?
cards.back: It increases by one carbon atom.
accept: It increases by one carbon atom.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In Br₂ addition, where does the first arrow from C=C point?
cards.back: To the bromine atom with induced δ⁺ charge.
accept: To the bromine atom with induced δ⁺ charge.
Towards the induced δ⁺ bromine atom.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Br₂ addition arrow 2: where do the Br–Br bonding electrons go?
cards.back: Towards the other Br, forming Br⁻.
accept: Towards the other Br, forming Br⁻.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Ethene + H₂SO₄: what breaks when ethene bonds to H⁺?
cards.back: The acid O–H bond breaks heterolytically to form HSO₄⁻.
accept: The acid O–H bond breaks heterolytically to form HSO₄⁻.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Complete the monomer: [–CH₂–CH(Cl)–]ₙ comes from ___
cards.back: CH₂=CHCl (chloroethene).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: During alcohol dehydration, which electrons form the new C=C bond?
cards.back: Electrons from a C–H bond on the adjacent carbon.
accept: Electrons from a C–H bond on the adjacent carbon.
A pair from a C–H bond next to the carbon losing water.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does a general formula represent in organic chemistry?
cards.back: The composition of a whole homologous series using a variable such as n.
accept: The composition of a whole homologous series using a variable such as n.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which type of radiation does the ozone layer absorb?
cards.back: Much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation.
accept: Much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which intermolecular forces act between poly(ethene) chains?
cards.back: London dispersion forces.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why do longer poly(ethene) chains usually have stronger attractions?
cards.back: More electrons and greater contact area increase London dispersion forces.
accept: More electrons and greater contact area increase London dispersion forces.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Name one common use of rigid, unplasticised PVC.
cards.back: Drainage pipes or window frames.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Name one common use of flexible, plasticised PVC.
cards.back: Electrical cable insulation.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which atmospheric gas made of hydrogen and oxygen absorbs Earth's infrared radiation?
cards.back: Water vapour (H₂O).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Give one typical use of Terylene polyester.
cards.back: Textile fibres, such as clothing fabric.
accept: Textile fibres, such as clothing fabric.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Give one typical use of nylon 6,6.
cards.back: Strong textile fibres or rope.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Give one typical use of Kevlar.
cards.back: Protective fabrics or high-strength reinforcing fibres.
accept: Protective fabrics or high-strength reinforcing fibres.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which groups form hydrogen bonds between typical polyamide chains?
cards.back: N–H groups donate to carbonyl oxygen atoms on other chains.
accept: N–H groups donate to carbonyl oxygen atoms on other chains.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What functional group forms when a nitrile group is reduced?
cards.back: A primary amine group, –CH₂NH₂.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What group replaces a nitro group on an aromatic ring upon reduction?
cards.back: An amino group, –NH₂, giving an aromatic amine.
accept: An amino group, –NH₂, giving an aromatic amine.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Name one use of superconductors in the AQA specification.
cards.back: Strong magnetic fields or lower energy losses in power transmission.
accept: Strong magnetic fields or lower energy losses in power transmission.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can a superconducting power cable reduce heating losses?
cards.back: It has zero electrical resistance below its critical temperature.
accept: It has zero electrical resistance below its critical temperature.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to resistance when a load is added in parallel?
cards.back: The combined resistance of that branch decreases.
accept: The combined resistance of that branch decreases.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can loading the lower part of a divider lower its output voltage?
cards.back: The parallel load lowers that branch resistance and its share of the supply p.d.
accept: The parallel load lowers that branch resistance and its share of the supply p.d.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is a fraction of crude oil?
cards.back: A mixture of hydrocarbons with similar boiling points.
accept: A mixture of hydrocarbons with similar boiling points.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is crude oil primarily a mixture of?
cards.back: Different hydrocarbons, mainly alkanes.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why are longer hydrocarbon fractions generally less volatile?
cards.back: Stronger intermolecular forces make them harder to vaporise.
accept: Stronger intermolecular forces make them harder to vaporise.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Give the catalytic-converter equation for CO and NO.
cards.back: 2CO + 2NO → 2CO₂ + N₂.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Where does sulfur dioxide in burning fossil fuels come from?
cards.back: Oxidation of sulfur-containing compounds or impurities in the fuel.
accept: Oxidation of sulfur-containing compounds or impurities in the fuel.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Where should cooling water enter a standard condenser?
cards.back: At the lower water inlet, keeping the jacket full.
accept: At the lower water inlet, keeping the jacket full.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the job of the condenser in distillation?
cards.back: To cool vapour so it condenses into a liquid.
accept: To cool vapour so it condenses into a liquid.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is bioethanol not automatically carbon neutral?
cards.back: Growing, processing and transporting feedstocks can release greenhouse gases.
accept: Growing, processing and transporting feedstocks can release greenhouse gases.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What happens to a divider resistor's effective resistance when loaded?
cards.back: It decreases: the load connects in parallel with that resistor.
accept: It decreases: the load connects in parallel with that resistor.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: If a load is connected across the lower divider resistor, output p.d.?
cards.back: It decreases for a fixed supply and unchanged upper resistor.
accept: It decreases for a fixed supply and unchanged upper resistor.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Define an alkene.
cards.back: An unsaturated hydrocarbon containing a C=C double bond.
accept: An unsaturated hydrocarbon containing a C=C double bond.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why did evidence lead to restrictions on CFCs?
cards.back: Scientists linked chlorine radicals from CFCs to stratospheric ozone loss.
accept: Scientists linked chlorine radicals from CFCs to stratospheric ozone loss.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is cracking commercially important?
cards.back: It converts less-demanded fractions into useful fuels and alkene feedstocks.
accept: It converts less-demanded fractions into useful fuels and alkene feedstocks.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is carbon monoxide harmful to humans?
cards.back: It binds to haemoglobin, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
accept: It binds to haemoglobin, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which environmental problem can sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides contribute to?
cards.back: Acid rain (acid deposition).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: In fluid motion, what is lift?
cards.back: A force from the fluid acting perpendicular to the direction of relative flow.
accept: A force from the fluid acting perpendicular to the direction of relative flow.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does air resistance generally change as an object's speed increases?
cards.back: It increases.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is breaking stress?
cards.back: The tensile stress when the material fractures: breaking force divided by original cross-sectional area.
accept: The tensile stress when the material fractures: breaking force divided by original cross-sectional area.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: State the principle of conservation of energy.
cards.back: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it is transferred between stores or systems.
accept: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it is transferred between stores or systems.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For n identical cells connected in series, what are the total emf and internal resistance?
cards.back: Total emf = nε; total internal resistance = nr.
accept: Total emf = nε; total internal resistance = nr.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For n identical cells connected in parallel, what are the total emf and internal resistance?
cards.back: Total emf = ε; total internal resistance = r/n.
accept: Total emf = ε; total internal resistance = r/n.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the terminal p.d. of a cell when no current flows?
cards.back: It equals the emf because the lost volts Ir are zero.
accept: It equals the emf because the lost volts Ir are zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does absorption affect a light signal in an optical fibre?
cards.back: Light energy is transferred to the fibre material, reducing signal intensity.
accept: Light energy is transferred to the fibre material, reducing signal intensity.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is seen at the centre of a white-light single-slit diffraction pattern?
cards.back: A white central maximum, with coloured side fringes.
accept: A white central maximum, with coloured side fringes.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a string fixed at both ends, how do harmonic frequencies relate to the first harmonic?
cards.back: The nth harmonic has frequency n times the first-harmonic frequency.
accept: The nth harmonic has frequency n times the first-harmonic frequency.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: In white-light double-slit interference, which colour has fringes further from the centre?
cards.back: Red, because its longer wavelength gives larger fringe spacing.
accept: Red, because its longer wavelength gives larger fringe spacing.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the baryon number of a quark and an antiquark?
cards.back: +⅓ for a quark; −⅓ for an antiquark.
accept: +⅓ for a quark; −⅓ for an antiquark.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What are the quarks in an antineutron?
cards.back: An anti-up quark and two anti-down quarks (anti-u, anti-d, anti-d).
accept: An anti-up quark and two anti-down quarks (anti-u, anti-d, anti-d).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the approximate rest energy of an electron or positron?
cards.back: 0.511 MeV for either particle.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How can uncertainty from a set of repeated readings be estimated using their range?
cards.back: Half the range: (highest reading − lowest reading)/2.
accept: Half the range: (highest reading − lowest reading)/2.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: When quoting a value and its absolute uncertainty, how should their decimal places compare?
cards.back: Quote the value to the same decimal place as its absolute uncertainty.
accept: Quote the value to the same decimal place as its absolute uncertainty.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: When is a graph's y-intercept consistent with zero?
cards.back: When zero lies within the plausible intercept range from acceptable lines.
accept: When zero lies within the plausible intercept range from acceptable lines.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: For a>1, what does y = af(x) do to y = f(x)?
cards.back: A vertical stretch by scale factor a.
accept: A vertical stretch by scale factor a.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What transformation maps y = f(x) to y = −f(x)?
cards.back: Reflection in the x-axis.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: For a>0, what does y = f(x+a) do to y = f(x)?
cards.back: Translate a units to the left.
accept: Translate a units to the left.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: For a positive integer n, what does n! mean?

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the factorial of zero (0!)?

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the binomial coefficient nCr as a factorial formula.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the general x^r term in (a+bx)^n for a positive integer n?
cards.back: nCr × a^(n−r) × (bx)^r.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: In the recurrence uₙ₊₁ = f(uₙ), how is the next term found?
cards.back: Substitute the previous term uₙ into f.
accept: Substitute the previous term uₙ into f.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: When is a sequence strictly increasing?
cards.back: When every term is greater than the previous one.
accept: When every term is greater than the previous one.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: For an upward-opening quadratic with two distinct roots, where is f(x)>0?
cards.back: Outside the roots.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What happens to an inequality sign when multiplying by a negative number?
cards.back: Reverse the inequality sign.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What are the asymptotes of y = k/x when k≠0?
cards.back: x = 0 and y = 0.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is true of the gradients of two non-vertical parallel lines?
cards.back: They are equal.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does a perpendicular from a circle's centre to a chord do?
cards.back: It bisects the chord.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the angle in a semicircle, subtended by its diameter?

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the exact value of sin 30°?

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the exact value of sin 45°?

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the exact value of cos 30°?

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the change-of-base formula for logₐx.
cards.back: logₐx = ln x / ln a (a>0, a≠1; x>0).
accept: logₐx = ln x / ln a (a>0, a≠1; x>0).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the first-principles definition of f′(x).
cards.back: lim(h→0) [f(x+h)−f(x)]/h.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: If the tangent gradient is m≠0, what is the normal gradient?

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does f′(x)>0 mean over an interval?
cards.back: The function is increasing there.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: How do position vectors give the vector from A to B?
cards.back: AB = OB − OA (position vectors).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does proof by deduction involve?
cards.back: Logical steps from stated assumptions to a justified conclusion.
accept: Logical steps from stated assumptions to a justified conclusion.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: On division of polynomial f(x) by (x−a), what is the remainder?
cards.back: f(a).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: How do you add 2D vectors (a,b) and (c,d)?
cards.back: (a+c, b+d).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is k times the vector (a,b)?
cards.back: (ka, kb).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: After using tan⁻¹(y/x) for a vector's angle, what should you check?
cards.back: The quadrant, using the signs of both components.
accept: The quadrant, using the signs of both components.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: In which quadrants is sin θ positive?
cards.back: Quadrants I and II.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: At which angles in degrees is tan θ undefined?
cards.back: 90° + 180°n, for any integer n.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What symmetry does the graph of cos x have?
cards.back: It is even: cos(−x)=cos x.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What symmetry does the graph of sin x have?
cards.back: It is odd: sin(−x)=−sin x.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: For total area where a graph crosses the x-axis, what is needed?
cards.back: Split at the roots and add the positive areas.
accept: Split at the roots and add the positive areas.

meta.note: Mechanics & Materials reported broad weakness; especially motion graphs, slope components, projectile motion and exact Newton law recall. Independent performance on harder practice has not yet been established. Advanced 16-question Mechanics bank available in exam practice (select Practice and Extended). Chemistry v40 adds syllabus-level esters, oils/fats, soaps, biodiesel, transesterification and carboxylic acids. These are review cards, not independently assessed performance. Acylation v41 covers acid anhydride/chloride and amide structure, 4 nucleophile classes, addition-elimination electron-flow theory and aspirin-related context. Mechanisms v42 includes electron-arrow interpretation for Year 1 organic reactions plus carbonyl nucleophilic addition and optical isomerism. Later separate aromatic and amine chapters remain unconfirmed for mock. Atomic structure v43 includes TOF mass spectrometry full stages, isotope spectra and weighted means, electron configuration to Z36, Period3/Group2 ionisation trends, and worked exam-style practice, with TOF self-reported revision priority. Guided answers are not independent marks. AQA 3.1.2 v44 comprehensive remainder: empirical/molecular formula, ideal gas equation, mass and gas stoichiometry, percentage yield/atom economy, ionic equations, hydrated salts, RP1 and direct/back titrations. All v44 cards are mock eligible; note explanations alone are not independent attainment. Electron-configuration exceptions (Cr/Cu and 4s electron removal) added as user-reported weak recall area on 25 October 2026; existing Cr/Cu and Fe ion cards upgraded to priority 9, plus 10 high-priority mock flashcards. No independent scored assessment yet. Period 3 first-ionisation-energy explanation highlighted for focused revision (Mg/Al 3s→3p subshell change; P/S paired-electron repulsion in 3p; overall trend with nuclear charge/shielding). Prioritized 5 existing cards and added 3 integrated-recall mock cards; user not independently tested. AQA 3.1.3 bonding v47: ionic formulas, dative and metallic models, six specified crystal examples and structure–property reasoning covered on mock cards. Bonding v48 covers VSEPR shapes 2–6 electron domains (lone-pair cases), polarity, London/permanent dipole/H bonds, water and ice density, exam-linked physics and chemistry explanations. Year 1 Energetics AQA 3.1.4: 65 targeted cards covering reaction enthalpy signs and definitions, calorimetry and RP2, standard formation/combustion enthalpies, Hess formation/combustion/hydration cycles, mean gaseous bond enthalpies; previously revised Born-Haber/entropy/Gibbs not duplicated. New content is notes/revision eligibility, not independently assessed mastery. Energetics v51: five targeted follow-up cards for calorimetry uncertainties, thermometer response, formation equation stoichiometry and diatomic bond enthalpy precision; three new original questions add 17 marks without repeating the combustion Hess and RP2 evaluations in v50. Bonding weakness focus v52 (26 Oct 2026): five individually testable compound-ion formulae and charges; high-priority unfamiliar VSEPR shapes, electronegativity/polarity, van der Waals' (induced dipole–dipole) comparisons, and four-mark explanation structures. AQA treats 'van der Waals', 'London' and 'dispersion' as synonyms here. Prior weak-area cards promoted; original study IDs retained. No independent marks earned by creating cards. Chemistry Energetics v53 focused weak-area programme: standard conditions/definitions, -q/n unit conversion and mole meaning, stoichiometric coefficients across calorimetry/Hess/bond enthalpies, Hess signs/paths and RP2 basic practical reasoning. New items are for revision, not independently assessed success. RP2 retained because paper 1/2 may assess practical skills even without Paper 3. Task 1 v122 first-pass Physics specification gap cards: short single-recall items (AS core and selected A2, optional Medical separated); original IDs preserved. Scope reflects taught vs future content. These are revision aids, not a certified exhaustive specification sign-off. | Year 1 Chemistry chat v126: 100 distinct short cards for the six newly taught topics (Kinetics, Equilibria, Redox, Periodicity, Group 2, Group 7), focused on missing reaction equations, formulas, explanations, calculations and RP3/RP4. Earlier Atomic Structure, Amount, Bonding, Energetics retained. Additions do not count as independently demonstrated mastery. | Updated five existing Group 7/Periodicity cards to classroom-preferred van der Waals' forces wording; retained London wording as accepted alternatives where present.
